<title>Asit v. Department of Information Technology - [2003] 35 SOT 230 (Indore - Trib.)</title>
<content>
ORDER

H.S. Sidhu, Judicial Member - This appeal filed by the revenue is directed against the order dated 14-8-2008 passed by the learned CIT(A)-I, Indore, for the assessment year 2005-06 on the following grounds:

"That the Id. CIT(A) erred in law and on facts in deleting the addition of Rs. 4,37,133 made by the Assessing Officer on account of excess stock found during the survey."

2. The briefly stated facts of the case are that a survey under section 133A of the Act was carried out in the business premises of the assessee on 16-12-2004. During the course of survey, a physical inventory of stock was taken and the stock of readymade garments was found at Rs. 14,04,363. The trading account of the business upto the date of survey was prepared and the value of stock as per books was arrived at Rs. 9,67,230. Thus, excess stock of Rs. 4,37,133 was found during the course of survey. The assessee’s statement was recorded in which he was asked to explain the difference in stock. The assessee has stated that the books of account of current year were not complete as the accountant was busy in finalising the audit for the previous year and there were certain purchases whose bills were not entered in the books. He further stated that he will verify the purchase bills and inform about the exact position of the stock and if any difference remained, he will pay tax on that. At the time of assessment proceedings, the assessee submitted before the Assessing Officer that the physical verification of stock was done at the time of survey but the values of items were taken on estimated basis. He also submitted that purchase of Rs. 4,68,913 was not entered in the books on the date of survey. The assessee submitted a list of such bills which are dated prior to 16-12-2004. The learned Assessing Officer, however, did not accept the contention of the assessee for the reason that the valuation was done in the presence of the assessee on the basis of price tags on the items. He was also not convinced with the argument of non-inclusion of purchase bills for the reason that no such bills were found during the survey and also the fact that some of the bills were having date much before the date of survey. He also found that some of the bills were related to cash purchases for which payments were not recorded in the books and, therefore, the same was also unexplained. He, therefore, added the entire difference of Rs. 4,37,133 to the total income of the assessee.

3. Being aggrieved, the assessee filed an appeal before the learned CIT(A) who deleted the addition by observing as under:

"I have considered the facts of the case and the contentions of the appellant. It is noted that the A.O. has added the difference between physical stock and book stock found during the survey. The appellant’s contention is that he had purchases of Rs. 4,68,913 which were not entered in the books. The A.O. has rejected this contention on the ground that these bills were not found during the survey and also that many of the bills were of dates much before the date of survey and it is not possible that these would remain unrecorded for such a long period. The A.O. has also pointed out that most of the purchases are in cash for which no cash entry was there in the books. In this connection, the appellant has stated that the books of the current year were not complete at the time of survey and he had made this statement during the survey itself. The fact that the books were not complete is also mentioned in the survey report. The list of bills which were not entered in the books was provided by the appellant before the A.O. A perusal of the list of bills shows that there were 32 bills from various parties. Most of the purchases are from outside Indore like Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Delhi, Ludhiana etc. It is seen that the A.O. has not made any inquiry about the genuineness of these bills. If the A.O. was not convinced about these bills, he should have made inquiries from the parties. Without making any inquiry, the A.O. cannot say that these bills are not genuine. It is also found that all these purchases have been entered by the appellant in the books subsequently and the books of account have been audited. The A.O. has not pointed out any defect in the books of account. The A.O. has also not rejected the books of account under section 145 of the Act. Without rejecting the books of account, no addition can be made on the basis of some observations made during the survey. It is also noted that the A.O. has accepted the results of the books of account for the remaining part of the year. Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the addition made by the A.O. is not justified. The same is accordingly deleted."

4. Against the order of the learned CIT(A), the revenue is in appeal before us.

5. Learned Departmental Representative relied on the order of the Assessing Officer and contended that the learned CIT(A) has deleted the addition without appreciating the facts that the assessee failed to produce the bills before the survey party and those bills were produced later on. It was also contended that some of the bills were of much older dates and hence the contention of the assessee that those were not entered in the books of account because the accountant was busy in other work, cannot be accepted.

6. Learned counsel for the assessee, on the other hand, supported the order of the learned CIT(A).

7. We have heard both the parties and gone through the records. In this case, the survey was conducted on 16-12-2004 and physical stock of Rs. 14,04,363 was found. As per books of account, the stock was worth Rs. 9,67,230. The difference of Rs. 4,37,133 was added as excess stock. At the time of survey, the assessee has categorically stated that the books of account were not complete and some of the purchase bills were not entered. During the course of assessment proceedings, the assessee has submitted the list of 32 bills totaling to Rs. 4,68,913 which were not entered in the books of account on the date of survey. The learned Assessing Officer, however, did not accept the contention of the assessee and did not even verify the genuineness of the bills. He added the amount only on the ground that the bills were not found during the course of survey. It is a fact that the books of account were not complete on the date of survey. The assessee has subsequently entered the bills in the books of account and get them audited. The learned Assessing Officer has not pointed out any defect in the books of account and has not rejected the books of account under section 145(3) of the Act. Without rejecting the books of account, the learned Assessing Officer cannot make the addition on the basis of the difference in the stock found during the survey especially when the assessee has explained the reasons for such difference. The learned CIT(A) has rightly held that the Assessing Officer could have verified the genuineness of the bills from the parties if he had any doubt about the same. We, therefore, find no infirmity in the order of the learned CIT(A) and the same is upheld.

8. In the result, the appeal of the revenue is dismissed.</content>
